title: attribution/v1 binding-record
description: Records that one session was bound to one task_run (the '1 session -> exactly 1 task' accounting principle -- see docs/protocols/attribution-v1.md). `binding_method` is a closed set that encodes the join-feasibility asymmetry between agents actually observed in a spike: Claude can be given a pre-assigned session_id up front, Codex can only be asked for its own thread_id after the fact, and a human's interactive session can only be bound by the human's own say-so. Hook-based binding is deliberately not in v1's closed set -- see docs/protocols/attribution-v1.md section 'Rejected designs' for why.

allOf.description: sol architect-review must5: schema-enforced, not just a verify-fixtures.mjs semantic check (kept as a defense-in-depth backstop -- see verify-fixtures.mjs).

binding_method.description: pre_assigned_session_id (Claude: wrapper generates a UUID nonce and passes it as the session_id itself via `claude -p --session-id <nonce>` -- no separate join step) | self_reported_thread_id (Codex: wrapper reads session_id from `codex exec --json`'s leading {"type":"thread.started",...} event, obtained after the fact -- never from a stderr banner) | manual_bind (an interactive session bound by explicit human action, e.g. `lane work bind --session-id`; a binding-record with this method MUST carry an `actor` whose kind is "human" -- schema-enforced via the top-level allOf/if-then above, with a matching verify-fixtures.mjs check kept as a defense-in-depth backstop, see docs/protocols/attribution-v1.md).

actor.description: Who performed this binding. Required, and required to have kind "human", when binding_method is manual_bind (see above) -- optional otherwise.
